title: SLA tiering and quality gates for hosted endpoints (PRD + launch checklist)
creator: Aisha K. Moreno
description:
Purpose: Define tiered SLA guarantees and an operational quality-gate framework for Redwood hosted endpoints (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) to enable predictable customer SLAs, safe progressive rollouts, and automated graded fallbacks. This PRD captures scope, success metrics, acceptance criteria, rollout strategy, rollback triggers, and cross-functional responsibilities.

Scope (in):
- Add three SLA tiers (Developer, Business, Enterprise) with documented latency and availability targets per endpoint class and request size.
- Define quality-gate checks (functional correctness, latency, token-cost, sample-based semantic quality) that must pass before traffic ramp.
- Implement canary and staged rollout policies integrated with Console rollouts and runtime routing.
- Instrument telemetry and synthetic tests required for gates (per-route p95/p99 latency, error-rate, semantic-regression score).
- Implement graded fallback matrix to substitute to compatible model variants or reduced feature profiles when gates fail.
- Publish customer-facing SLA doc and an internal runbook for SRE/SEs.

Out of scope (for this ticket): private/VPC-only enforcement, dedicated capacity billing plumbing, and multi-region active failover (will be tracked separately).

Stakeholders: PM (Aisha K. Moreno), Eng (Ethan Park, runtime & routing), SRE (Maya R. Chen), Console (Diego Alvarez), QA (Priya Singh), Legal/Compliance (for SLA wording).

Success metrics:
- 99.95% availability for Enterprise tier over 30-day window for standard requests (<=1024 tokens).
- p95 latency within tier targets for >=95% of traffic.
- Zero P0 incidents during first 10k Enterprise endpoint-hours attributable to rollout strategy.
- Automated quality gates block <1% of legitimate rollouts after initial stabilization window (false-positive rate).
acceptance_criteria: SLA definitions: Developer/Business/Enterprise tiers published with numeric p50/p95/p99 latency and availability thresholds per endpoint type.
Telemetry: per-route dashboards exist showing p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, token-cost, and semantic-regression score; synthetic canary suite runs every 15 minutes.
Quality gates: a gating service is available that evaluates new rollout artifacts against functional tests, latency budget, and semantic evaluation before increasing traffic.

Canary behavior: canary traffic begins at 0.1% and can be programmatically advanced to 1%, 5%, 20% if and only if gate checks pass at each step; failure triggers automatic rollback to previous model variant.

Fallbacks: for model timeouts or elevated token-cost, runtime must route to a compatible quantized model variant or a reduced-profile endpoint without dropping existing sessions. Fallback behavior is configurable per-customer and documented.

E2E tests: end-to-end smoke tests for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank with structured-output and function-calling are added to CI and pass in staging; PRs that change the gating logic include test coverage.
Operational runbook: documented runbook with rollback steps, metrics to watch, and postmortem checklist exists in Confluence and is reviewed by SRE and Support.
Legal/Subscription: SLA terms drafted and approved by Legal for public cloud customers and signposted in Console billing UI for Enterprise tier.
Security: key telemetry data used for gates conforms to PII policy and KMS is used for sensitive logs; security signoff attached to the ticket.

Performance baseline: a pre-roll baseline report for each endpoint type (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) within supported request-size buckets is stored in the performance datastore and linked from the ticket.
launch_checklist: Finalize SLA numerical targets and publish to internal doc + public page.
Implement and test synthetic canary suite in staging against the new gating service.
Add per-route telemetry panels to Console and configure alerting thresholds for p95/p99 and error-rate.
Deliver UI controls for staged rollouts (0.1/1/5/20%) with audit logging and operator override.
Wire automatic rollback hooks from gating service into runtime routing controller.
Create customer communication templates (email + Console banner) for SLA opt-in and upgrade path.
Legal signoff on SLA language; product and finance signoff on Enterprise billing flow.
Run 48h soak with Business-tier traffic profile in a pre-prod cluster and validate SLO compliance metrics.
Perform chaos-monkey tests (node loss, GPU OOM, model-copy delay) to validate fallback behavior.
Run a canary to 10 pilot customers and collect telemetry for 7 days before wide release.
Finalize support runbook and ensure on-call rotations cover first 14 days of Enterprise SLA availability window.
Produce a post-launch health dashboard and a triage playbook for semantic regressions detected by eval hooks.
decision_log: 2025-11-12: Agreed to three-tier SLA model (Developer/Business/Enterprise) to balance cost and expectations.
2026-01-07: Approved gating thresholds — initial semantic-regression threshold set to a 2% delta vs baseline eval suite; will adjust after pilot.
2026-02-02: Chose fallback strategy to prefer compatible quantized model variants over region failover to reduce cross-region complexity.
2026-02-28: Decided to keep private/VPC enforcement out of scope for MVP; will add hooks for future enforcement.
notes:
Scope changes and tradeoffs log:
- 2025-12-01: Removed multi-region active failover from this ticket to avoid coupling with infra network migration (tracked in ENG-4123).
- Tradeoff: requiring semantic eval gate prior to rollout increases time-to-deploy for large models; mitigations include parallelized eval runners and an initial permissive mode for Developer tier.
- Risk: false-positive gate failures could block important rollouts. QA will produce a tuned set of check-suites and an 'operator bypass' flow with explicit audit logging for critical customer fixes.
- Follow-ups: add per-customer SLA overrides and a cost-estimator in Console (new ticket to be created after pilot).
